nodes.label: Three-layer separation: core, render, ui
nodes.rationale: The package is split so geometry and document logic can be tested without a display, every GL call lives in one place, and Qt panels never reach into widgets they do not own.

nodes.label: core never imports Qt
nodes.rationale: All geometry and document logic stays testable without a display, which is exactly what the pytest suite exercises.

nodes.label: render owns every GL call
nodes.rationale: The viewport hands the renderer a camera and a settings object and gets a frame back. The renderer also restores neutral GL state, because the 2D overlay is painted with QPainter on the same context.

nodes.label: Panels edit dataclasses, never foreign widgets
nodes.rationale: Panels mutate the settings held by ViewerState and emit a change signal; the viewport listens and repaints. No panel reaches into another panel's widgets.
nodes.norm_label: panels edit dataclasses, never foreign widgets

nodes.label: Every document edit is a command
nodes.rationale: Four generic commands -- set attributes, add, remove, replace -- cover measurements, annotations and bookmarks alike, so undo needs no new code when a new kind of object turns up.
nodes.norm_label: every document edit is a command

nodes.label: Measurements drawn in screen space with QPainter
nodes.rationale: Screen-space drawing gives reliable line thickness and antialiasing on every driver, keeps the numbers legible in front of the model, and makes the text labels free.
nodes.norm_label: measurements drawn in screen space with qpainter

nodes.label: Annotations drawn as widened geometry
nodes.rationale: Paint on the back of the model has to be hidden by it, so strokes are real geometry. Each segment is a quad the vertex shader widens in screen space, keeping the brush a constant pixel width at any zoom -- something glLineWidth cannot promise on a core profile.

nodes.label: Morton-curve leaf boxes for picking
nodes.rationale: Every click, hover and painted sample casts a ray, so picking speed decides whether a large scan still feels direct. Triangles are sorted along a Morton curve into leaf boxes; a ray tests every box in one vectorised sweep and intersects only the triangles in the leaves it entered -- about 0.5 ms per ray against 90 ms brute force on a half-million-triangle mesh.

nodes.label: Camera motion is deliberately not undoable
nodes.rationale: Orbiting is a gesture rather than an edit, and burying real changes under a hundred camera steps is what makes undo useless in a 3D viewer.
nodes.norm_label: camera motion is deliberately not undoable

nodes.label: Units are adopted, never guessed
nodes.rationale: glTF is the one common format that declares its unit -- metres -- so the measurement panel adopts it. OBJ and STL declare nothing, so nothing is guessed.

nodes.label: Orthographic extent derived from FOV and distance
nodes.rationale: Deriving the extent from the field of view and distance keeps the object the same size on screen when the projection is switched.
nodes.norm_label: orthographic extent derived from fov and distance

nodes.label: High Quality without ray tracing
nodes.rationale: A shadow map, a depth-and-normal pre-pass and one occlusion pass cost a few milliseconds between them, so the view stays live while it is orbited. Neither effect traces a ray.

nodes.label: The pedestal is ordinary geometry so it catches the shadow
nodes.rationale: Because the disc is real geometry rather than a drawn guide it receives the cast shadow -- which is what makes contact and height readable.
nodes.norm_label: the pedestal is ordinary geometry so it catches the shadow

nodes.label: The cut interior is flooded flat
nodes.rationale: Flooding the exposed interior with a flat colour makes the cut read as solid material rather than as a hollow shell, and the profile at the cut is traced as a bright contour.
nodes.norm_label: the cut interior is flooded flat

nodes.label: REFVIEW_RESOURCES resource override
nodes.rationale: Pointing REFVIEW_RESOURCES at another directory lets an artist use their own matcap and model library without touching the package.

nodes.label: PySide6 pinned below 6.8
nodes.rationale: Newer Qt builds need a more recent MSVC runtime than many Windows machines have installed, and fail with 'DLL load failed while importing QtCore'.

nodes.label: Tag-driven desktop releases
nodes.rationale: Pushing a tag such as v1.1.0 builds self-contained archives for Windows, Intel macOS and Apple Silicon macOS, which the release workflow publishes automatically.

nodes.label: Semantic versioning policy
nodes.rationale: The minor number moves when features land, the patch number when only fixes do.

nodes.label: STL corner welding
nodes.rationale: STL stores three loose corners per facet, so corners are welded on import and a printed part arrives with shared vertices instead.

nodes.label: High Quality shading mode (1.1.0)
nodes.rationale: Soft shadows and screen-space ambient occlusion are approximations rather than traced rays, so a full frame costs a few milliseconds and the view stays live.

nodes.label: Model orientation (1.1.0)
nodes.rationale: Formats disagree about which axis points up and STL says nothing, so the turn is applied once to the mesh as a plain rotation, and measurements and annotations are carried through it so marks stay where they were put.

nodes.label: Shift-snapped orbiting (1.1.0)
nodes.rationale: The snapped angle is measured from where the drag started, so releasing Shift resumes the free orbit without a jump.

nodes.label: Picking about a hundred times faster
nodes.rationale: On a half-million-triangle scan a pick went from about 90 ms to 0.5 ms, which is what keeps hovering, measuring and painting responsive.
nodes.norm_label: picking about a hundred times faster

nodes.label: Every panel scrolls
nodes.rationale: A tab taller than the dock -- the Shading tab on a laptop -- no longer has its rows squashed or cut off, and the matcap gallery sits above a draggable handle instead of a fixed height.

nodes.label: Session format version 4
nodes.rationale: Version 4 carries the section, pedestal, high-quality, navigation and orientation settings, and files written by 1.0 still load.

nodes.label: Query the graph before reading source
nodes.rationale: query, path and explain return a scoped subgraph, usually much smaller than the full report or raw grep output.

nodes.label: Terracotta clay matcap
nodes.rationale: 512x512 analytic sphere render on a matching flat backdrop. Matte terracotta base with an almost invisible specular lobe, key light from the upper left and a cool dim fill from the lower right; the silhouette darkens to a soft rim. This is the sculpting default: no highlight to compete with the form, so surface transitions read as clay.

nodes.label: Charcoal matcap
nodes.rationale: 512x512 analytic sphere render, very dark low-key base against a blue-grey backdrop. Two distinct broad highlights are visible -- the warm key at the upper left and the cool fill at the lower right -- which is what keeps a near-black surface readable.

nodes.label: Jade matcap
nodes.rationale: 512x512 analytic sphere render in saturated green with a soft, wide specular lobe and noticeable fill bounce, giving a translucent stone look rather than a plastic one.

nodes.label: Steel matcap
nodes.rationale: 512x512 analytic sphere render, neutral grey with a small, intensely bright specular hotspot and a strong cool rim -- the low-roughness end of the bundled set. The tight highlight makes high-frequency surface noise obvious, which is how it reads dents and tool marks.

nodes.label: Studio white matcap
nodes.rationale: 512x512 analytic sphere render, bright near-neutral base with a broad soft highlight and a long gradient into shadow. The high key level flattens fine detail and shows large-form volume, the opposite trade to the steel matcap.

nodes.label: Wax skin matcap
nodes.rationale: 512x512 analytic sphere render, warm pink base with a warm red fill instead of the cool default, and a very soft falloff -- a waxy, subsurface-like look for figure work.

links.source_location: Two overlays solving the same 'mark the model' problem by opposite means, sharing no code: one is 3D geometry so the model can occlude it, the other is 2D so it never can.
Both are the same refusal to guess what a file does not state: the axis convention and the unit.
The pedestal only pays for itself once something casts a shadow onto it, so the two features were added together and are read together.
Both are defences against Windows binary incompatibility -- one against the MSVC runtime, the other against a mixed conda/pip BLAS.
The same graph-first rule written twice, once per agent host.
Opposite ends of the same trade: a tight hotspot that exposes high-frequency detail against a broad key that shows large-form volume.
